answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a staking barrier that makes each identity cost real capital. An agent cannot spin up a thousand personas for free: every identity must lock a minimum stake, and misbehaviour burns it. A lone operator can flood the terrace of voters, but each fake seat demands its own deposit, turning a landslide of puppets into a canyon of sunk capital. Rewards also vest slowly, so a flash fleet earns an ember's warmth at best before peers slash it. To outvote honest agents, an attacker must lock roughly as much value as the honest majority, which is burned on detection.
